title: Motif line with the project's psc-motif-zigzag-3pt.pmf at 5 x 8 mm, spacing 2 mm, run pitch 3 mm
description: The 40 x 40 mm square of line-motif-zigzag-5x8 with the motif line's Run pitch at 3 mm, everything else the same (#1068). At 3 mm PE-DESIGN splits each 3.2 mm motif stitch in two (117 stitches); at 7 mm it sews as at 5 (75 in its status bar, 76 by OpenStitch's reader).

evidence.note: Motif Stitch (line and region): pattern, size, arrange, spacing, row offset, run pitch

PE-DESIGN 11.50 reference stitches/1068-motif-5x8-runpitch-3p0.pes (the coordinator's round 15 capture, 2026-11-14, made from 608-motif-5x8 with only Run pitch changed): 117 stitches by OpenStitch's reader, 40,00 x 40,00 mm; its header lists only the project's motif

references.make: Programmable Stitch Creator, New Motif Pattern: click the base line to add a point, drag it to (512,768); Save As psc-motif-zigzag-3pt.pmf (round 4). Layout & Editing, 100 x 100 mm page: Home > Shapes > Rectangle, a 40 x 40 mm square; region Not Sewn; line Motif Stitch > that file, Maintain aspect ratio off, motif 5,0 mm wide (the lower field, horizontal arrow) and 8,0 mm high (the upper field, vertical arrow), H-Arrange and V-Arrange first buttons, Offset 0,0, Spacing 2,0, Run pitch 3,0, Start/End Type Feed. Save As PES (default type).

measurements.evidence: PE-DESIGN 11.50 sews 117 needle points: the motifs around the square, the 2 mm runs between them and the line's tie-in and lock, the motif stitches split at a pitch under their 3.2 mm
the motifs stay on the square's outline

a motif's stitch: half its 5 mm length along the outline and 2.0 mm across

PE-DESIGN's longest is 2.10 mm, 2.1 mm of run into the start point; ours is 2.36 mm, at the top-left corner. PE-DESIGN cuts each corner with a motif ((0, 3.3) to (3.2, 3.1) to (3.8, 0) mm from the corner), ours runs a motif into it; 608-motif-5x8 at Run pitch 5 shows the same, apart from #1068, so 0.3 mm until motif corners are matched
